gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-adlam: Noto Sans Adlam keeps its curve endings well apart. Over a long page its tall, full c, s and z give the text a generous, open texture, while Origami's brushed single-stroke headings stay firmly in charge above it.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-lisu: Marker-traced lines, poured-lead mass. Origami draws everything in monoline strokes for loud personality, whereas Noto Sans Lisu is a plain sans that keeps tiny gaps under its ascenders and lets wide s curves do the quiet work.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-saira: Hollow glass-tube letters, glowing and constant. Make Origami small and that tube effect gets cramped, while Saira, a sans-serif with see-through s shapes, would feel stretched if you blew it up large.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-sarpanch: Cord-thick curves, heavy as the stems. Sarpanch is a plain sans with a clearly open e and compact ascender spacing, so a longer passage moves along with an approachable, tidy rhythm under Origami's chunky headings.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-sulphur-point: Brushed sign-painter strokes meet bulky, marker-like text. Sulphur Point's distinct open gaps in c, e, s and a give this sans a sturdy steadiness that lets Origami be the loud, poured-lead one.
